title: Branching from snapshots: Monte Carlo values and turn-level credit
design_ref: Credit assignment: a ladder of methods; Branching rollouts
purpose: Pick multi-bug trajectories, failed and successful, one per task (the failed ones from tasks the model solves at least once, so a better decision existed), and give the credit worker four branches per branch point. It must compute the value of the state after each branch point, turn the differences into per-turn advantages, and find the decisive segment; on a failed trajectory a successful branch shows which decision mattered. Branches must share their prefix in the rollout engine's cache.

steps.display: vLLM /metrics during the branch rollouts: prefix cache
environment time: branches vs the trajectories they credit
steps.output: branches 1613 s for 6 trajectories whose own episodes took 453 s

checks.description: every chosen trajectory got values at its branch points from four verified continuations each
checks.because: One Indexed Job of four branch pods per point, on the low-priority branch queue; each branch ends with the verifier's fresh-environment check.

checks.description: turn-level advantages differ between turns of the same trajectory, unlike trajectory-level ones
checks.because: Each segment gets V(after) - V(before); trajectory-level gives every turn the same number.

checks.description: on at least one failed trajectory a branch succeeded, so a state on the failed path still had value
checks.because: A failing trajectory with one successful branch shows which decision turned failure into success.

checks.description: branches reused their shared prefix from the rollout engine's cache
checks.because: Every branch from a point sends the same message prefix; vLLM's prefix cache serves those tokens without recomputing them.

notes: Prefix cache hit rate during branching: 97%. Branch environment time 1613 s against 453 s for the trajectories themselves.
